title: ASPIRIN - Acetylsalicylic acid versus placebo in addition to a local non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug in the treatment of thrombotic episodes in superficial venous malformations in children aged 6 to 17 years: a controlled randomised, double-blind, cross-over, multicenter trial
official: ASPIRIN - Acetylsalicylic acid versus placebo in addition to a local non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug in the treatment of thrombotic episodes in superficial venous malformations in children aged 6 to 17 years: a controlled randomised, double-blind, cross-over, multicenter trial
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of per os acetylsalicylic acid versus placebo, in addition to a local non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, on the pain associated with superficial venous thrombosis in children with superficial venous malformations
conditions: Thrombotic episodes in superficial venous malformations in children

interventions.name: DICLOFENAC ARROW 1 %, gel en flacon pressurisé

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients aged 6 to 17 included
2. Weight ≥ 20 kg
3. Isolated or combined superficial venous malformation, whatever the topography, confirmed by imaging (MRI, CT, Doppler ultrasound), with the presence of phleboliths indicating the occurrence of previous superficial venous thrombosis
4. Complicated by acute thrombotic episodes (2 or more in the previous 12 months)
5. Written consent of the child's legal representatives or of the participant if over 18 years of age
6. Affiliation of a social security scheme
7. Highly effective contraception for young women of childbearing age
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with deep or syndromic venous malformation
2. Patients with known G6PD deficiency
3. Patients with known mastocytosis
4. History of hemarthrosis
5. Simultaneous participation in another biomedical study
6. Constitutional or acquired haemostasis pathology
7. Current treatment affecting haemostasis (anticoagulants, platelet anti-aggregants, oral NSAIDs)
8. Frequent bleeding (epistaxis, other) requiring management
9. Basic treatment of venous malformation (mTOR inhibitor)
10. Active neoplasia or infection (altered coagulation balance)
11. Known allergy to acetylsalicylic acid
12. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose or galactose malabsorption syndrome
13. Known allergy to NSAIDs
14. Patient with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome or Cloves syndrome
15. History of peptic ulcer disease or chronic gastritis
16. History of asthma, angioedema, urticaria, or acute rhinitis triggered by diclofenac, acetylsalicylic acid, or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
17. Allergy to one of the excipients of diclofenac gel
18. Injured skin, whatever the lesion: oozing dermatitis, eczema, infected lesions, burns or wounds
19. Pregnant and breastfeeding women
20. Severe renal insufficiency, severe hepatic insufficiency, severe uncontrolled cardiac insufficiency
21. Methotrexate ≥ 20 mg/week
